CANDIDATES.title: IVC 135 — inflowing IVC in 3D
CANDIDATES.note: One of only three |v_dev| > 40 km/s clouds in the local disk–halo interface; low N_HI/A_V suggests a disk origin. Northern, high latitude. O'Neill+26: d = 745 pc, z = 606 pc, v_LSR -47.0, v_dev -44.6 km/s, R_eff 68.2 pc, 196 deg².

CANDIDATES.combo: LLIV Arch — the largest deviation velocity
CANDIDATES.title: LLIV Arch — the largest deviation velocity
CANDIDATES.note: The Low-Latitude Intermediate-Velocity Arch mapped in 3D for the first time; inflowing at −53 km/s, 1 kpc away, 1.5×10⁴ M☉. O'Neill+26: d = 996 pc, z = 606 pc, v_LSR -53.4, v_dev -47.2 km/s, R_eff 94.5 pc, 180 deg².

CANDIDATES.title: IVC 210 — molecular IVC at 555 pc
CANDIDATES.note: Third true IVC (IV18 / G211+63); the nearest of the three and the lowest z (482 pc). O'Neill+26: d = 555 pc, z = 482 pc, v_LSR -47.0, v_dev -47.9 km/s, R_eff 46.3 pc, 118 deg².

CANDIDATES.combo: Draco cloud — IV Arch meets the disk?
CANDIDATES.title: Draco cloud — IV Arch meets the disk?
CANDIDATES.note: Classic molecular IVC at 516 pc, 320 pc above the plane; shares the IV Arch's velocity but sits far below it — a candidate leading edge of the Arch–disk encounter ([CII] detection). O'Neill+26: d = 516 pc, z = 319 pc, v_LSR -22.5, v_dev -24.4 km/s, R_eff 38.7 pc, 80 deg².

CANDIDATES.title: Cloud 2066 — outflowing, never catalogued
CANDIDATES.note: Highest positive deviation velocity in the O'Neill+26 sample (+32 km/s) at z = 613 pc; a jagged chain of clumps not present in any IVC catalog. O'Neill+26: d = 899 pc, z = 613 pc, v_LSR 23.8, v_dev 32.5 km/s, R_eff 98.8 pc, 285 deg².

CANDIDATES.title: Kepler field — parallax ladder
CANDIDATES.note: Best 1° field inside the 15° Kepler survey region (Via KRS tiles): 13 rungs from Kepler-field Gaia stars with overlapping parallax error bars — a dense local ladder at 0.1–5 kpc.

CANDIDATES.title: M31 tiling region (6°)
CANDIDATES.note: Centre of the 6° M31 survey cone: extragalactic backlights (M31 halo + background) behind the Galactic foreground at b = −22°; overlaps the planned tiling.

CANDIDATES.title: M82 tiling region (2°)
CANDIDATES.note: The 2° M82 cone: high-latitude sightline between the LLIV Arch (10° away) and the Local-Bubble-shell cirrus G139.6+47.6 (7° away); overlaps the planned tiling.

CANDIDATES.title: Densest bright backlights (G ≤ 18, 1°)
CANDIDATES.note: 760 stream stars brighter than G = 18 in one 1° pointing (Sgr only); 2 rungs — fibers will not be the limit here.

CANDIDATES.title: Strongest HVC gas over a multi-rung field

CANDIDATES.title: Widest halo-star distance spread
CANDIDATES.note: 1264 individual halo stars (KG 1160, RRL 42, BHB 62) spanning 3.4–79.2 kpc in 17 20 %-wide distance bins — a ladder built from single stars rather than structures.

CANDIDATES.title: Most halo stars beyond 50 kpc
CANDIDATES.note: 670 halo stars past 50 kpc (875 total, 14 distance bins; KG 0, RRL 875, BHB 0) — the outer-halo end of the ladder.

CANDIDATES.title: Palomar 5 and its tidal tails
CANDIDATES.note: A globular cluster (23 kpc) with 20°-long tidal tails: cluster + stream at one distance plus the Sgr stream behind; HI profiled along the tails in hi_along_streams.png.

CANDIDATES.title: Sculptor dSph behind the Magellanic Stream
